Subject: Partial-month GPU add-on charge on invoice #7423 - request for proration and VAT handling

Hi Stephanie,

We just received invoice #7423 and noticed a line for 'GPU ephemeral add-on' covering 2026-11-01 to 2026-12-31. We only enabled the burst capacity on 2026-11-10 and turned it off on 2026-11-23. Could you confirm how that charge was calculated? We expected a prorated amount for 13 days of usage, not the full month.

Also, because Novaforce is EU-registered and registered for reverse-charge, we need the invoice to reflect reverse-charge VAT (zero-rate on your side) and include our VAT number for bookkeeping. I attached our VAT certificate for reference.

Quick ask: can you either (a) issue a corrected invoice showing the prorated amount and reverse-charge handling, or (b) issue a credit note for the overcharge and a corrected replacement invoice? We need this by end of week to close our month-end.

Thanks,
Hans
Procurement Manager
Novaforce Systems

Hi all,

I've pulled the billing record and attached a draft credit note plus a corrected invoice. Calculation notes:
- Original GPU add-on monthly line: EUR 3,200 (full month).
- Active days billed by system: 23 days (11/01–11/23) but your reported enablement was 11/10–11/23 (14 days). We reconciled logs and will honor the 14-day window.
- Daily rate used: EUR 3,200 / 30 = EUR 106.67/day.
- Prorated charge for 14 days = EUR 1,493.38.
- Credit to issue = EUR 3,200 - EUR 1,493.38 = EUR 1,706.62.

Action options (pick one):
1) Issue credit note for EUR 1,706.62 now (DocuSign link below) and issue corrected invoice reflecting prorated GPU add-on and reverse-charge VAT statement.
2) Reissue corrected invoice and apply the credit on next billing cycle (no immediate payment move).

DocuSign (credit note draft): https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABC123-nova-credit
Draft credit note filename: draft-credit-note-RDW-9483.pdf
Corrected invoice filename: 202611-corrected-invoice-7423.pdf

I've also attached our standard reverse-charge template wording; Marcus, can you confirm the exact invoice wording.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
